info.title: Tap
info.description: tap — ngrok-style HTTP inspector with optional Cloudflare tunnels. Install as a global .NET tool: `dotnet tool install -g Tap`. Run `tap --help` to get started.

commands.name: install-cloudflared
commands.description: Install the cloudflared binary via the host's package manager

commands.name: run
commands.description:
Start the inspector and optionally a Cloudflare tunnel in front of an upstream
URL. With no args, lists saved profiles

options.name: --quick
options.description:
Spin up a TryCloudflare quick
tunnel and route it through the
inspector

options.name: --api-managed
options.description:
Use the Cloudflare API to
create/reuse a named tunnel and
route HOSTNAME through it

options.name: --dynamic
options.description:
Mint a fresh hostname under ZONE
(uses --api-managed; pair with
--account/--api-token)

options.name: --docker
options.description:
Run cloudflared in a Docker
container
(cloudflare/cloudflared:latest)
it via the host's package manager

options.name: --auto-install
options.description:
If cloudflared is missing, install
it via the host's package manager

options.name: --auth-header
options.description:
Require an API key in this header
on the proxy

options.name: --config
options.description:
Optional tap.config JSON file to
load defaults from

options.name: --verbose
options.description:
Show ASP.NET Core framework logs
alongside the request log

options.name: --name
options.description:
Run a named profile from
~/.config/tap/tunnels (or
%APPDATA%/tap/tunnels). CLI flags
override profile values

arguments.name: UPSTREAM
arguments.description:
Upstream URL to inspect/forward to (e.g.
http://localhost:3000). May also be set via tap.config or env
TAP_UPSTREAM

commands.name: save
commands.description: Save a named tunnel profile to %APPDATA%/tap/tunnels (or ~/.config/tap/tunnels)
